title: Repeated cubic graph-factor transport boundary
question: Do the two-sided one-factor Q3 graph bounds with A^(-3/4) control imply a uniform repeated product, or is an additional A-power transport theorem required?
method: Define the finite positive diagonal family A_n=diag(1,2^(4n),2^(8n)) and the raising shift S on three basis vectors.
Set Q_n=S A_n^(3/4) using the exact integer diagonal entries 1,2^(3n),2^(6n).
Compute both one-factor infinity norms and the repeated product norm with exact rational matrix arithmetic for n=1,2,3.
Reproduce the scale identities and inequalities in an independent lane and Lean R229.
finding: The one-factor norms are 1 and 2^(-3n), while the repeated target norm is 2^(3n)=8^n. Separate one-factor A^(-3/4) bounds therefore do not yield a volume- or history-uniform repeated-factor bound.
decision_reason: This is a new linkage after EXP-001045/1046: it isolates repeated A-power composition, rather than the already-recorded one-site-to-mixed marginal failure or the prescribed polynomial-word degree escalation.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite operator inference boundary. It rejects only the naive repeated-factor inference and does not reject stronger Q3-specific transport, analytic/Frechet, or cancellation routes.

adversarial_review.check: Q_n is a finite operator witness and is not identified with the Q3 multiplier.
Both one-sided graph norms are retained with their distinct exact values.
All powers are exact integer powers of the base; no floating point is used.
The product target is a minimal naive composition, not a universal requirement for every topology.
R229 covers fixture arithmetic only, not unbounded operator domains.
No common alpha, KMS/OS, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A result is claimed.

qft_interface.closed: A finite repeated-factor transport boundary before the common-alpha interface.
qft_interface.open: Actual Q3 history, first passage, exhaustion, common alpha, KMS, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
